meta.title: File:The mantapa of the Hoysaleswara Temple.jpg
meta.desc: The mantapa of the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu is a large, open pillared hall that serves as the main congregational space for devotees. It is supported by lathe-turned pillars, a hallmark of Hoysala craftsmanship, which are polished, symmetrical, and precisely shaped using a lathe technique to create uniform cylindrical forms with intricate fluting and decorative motifs.

meta.title: File:Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.jpg
meta.desc: The Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu (12th century) is anarchitectural marvel of Hoysala architecture, built in chloritic schist with a stellate (star-shaped) plan that maximizes sculptural surfaces. It features a sanctum, vestibule, and mandapa with lathe-turned pillars, intricately carved ceilings, and exterior walls covered in deep-relief panels depicting deities and epics.

meta.title: File:Shiva and Parvati relief at Hoysaleswara temple.jpg

meta.title: File:Mandapa of Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: The open mandapa of the Hoysaleshwara Temple at Halebidu, built in the distinctive Hoysala architectural tradition. The structure stands on a raised platform and features elaborately carved pillars, stone ceilings and sculpted architectural members. This photograph shows the mandapa from the side, with its richly ornamented stone elements and paved circumambulatory area visible.

meta.title: File:Carved Pillars of Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: A row of intricately carved stone pillars at the Hoysaleshwara Temple in Halebidu, showcasing the refined craftsmanship of Hoysala architecture. The pillars combine geometric mouldings with rounded and faceted sections, while the surrounding stonework carries additional decorative details.

meta.title: File:Lathe-Turned Pillar at Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: A richly finished lathe-turned stone pillar inside the Hoysaleshwara Temple at Halebidu, a 12th-century Hoysala monument dedicated to Shiva. The temple is renowned for its finely carved soapstone architecture and sculptural detailing. This photograph highlights the polished circular mouldings of the pillar, adjoining carved supports and the stone railing overlooking the temple grounds.

Built in 1133 CE during the reign of Vishnuvardhana, the Jain temple demonstrates the sophisticated craftsmanship of Hoysala builders. The closely spaced columns create a rhythmic arrangement throughout the mandapa.

meta.title: File:Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: Hoysaleshwara Temple is a 12th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva at Halebidu, Karnataka, the former capital of the Hoysala Empire. Built in soapstone, it is a twin-shrine temple with richly carved exterior walls depicting deities, dancers, animals and scenes from Hindu epics. The temple is renowned for its intricate Hoysala architecture, star-shaped plan and finely detailed sculptural frieze

meta.title: File:Carved Exterior of Hoysaleshwara Temple, Halebidu, Karnataka.jpg
meta.desc: A wider view of the richly carved exterior of Hoysaleshwara Temple at Halebidu. The temple walls feature multiple horizontal friezes, sculptural panels, miniature architectural forms and projecting sections arranged across the surface. The photograph shows how the Hoysala style combines a complex temple plan with an exceptionally elaborate sculptural treatment of the exterior.
